conventions.positions: mm from the trim box's top-left corner (y down)
conventions.dist: n, min, p10, median, p90, max
conventions.L: one body leading of the text involved (else the page's body leading)
conventions.page_types: front = carries the nameplate; back = far end of its section; inside = the rest

bleed_mm.note: the press PDFs carry no bleed: MediaBox = TrimBox = BleedBox; nothing is printed beyond the trim

inside_vs_outside_mm.rule: recto = odd reading index within the section (inside margin = left); verso = even (inside = right)

type_area_mm.source: 8-column lattice fitted to body frames (published1/headlines.py estimate_grids)

story_text_columns.rule: side-by-side body frames of one width, one gutter apart, chained; M frames whose total width is an N-column span (+-1.5 mm): the story's text is set in M equal columns across N grid columns, width = (N x col + (N - 1) x gutter - (M - 1) x gutter) / M

not_on_a_span.note: single frames narrower or wider than any column set: text in boxes (inset) or wrapped around pictures

variant_6col.derived: same type area and gutter as the 8-column grid
variant_6col.note: its 50 mm column is the 4-grid-columns-in-3 (and 8-in-6) case of story_text_columns

grid.source: published1 body frames (corrected.json) chained into column sets; headline span fit from headlines.jsonl

body.first_line_indent_source: paragraphs.jsonl (668 verified paragraphs on these pages)
body.story_first_line_rule: first body line of each story (story_openings); datelines counted apart
body.source: published1 body frames (corrected.json): size, leading, h-scale, word space ratio, tracking, line classes

headline_brief.definition: brief headlines inside a text flow (H4)

byline.definition: bylines on their own line (B1 line, B2)

dateline.definition: run-in dateline: a colon, or a spaced dash, within 30 mm of the start of a story's first body line (story_openings); bold = a bold face or text render mode 2

headline_size.rule: span = the headline's fitted grid span (headlines.py); sizes in pt; page type columns per section

headline_to_deck.measure: B2B: headline last baseline -> deck first baseline

byline_to_body.measure: B2B: byline line -> first body baseline

headline_to_body.measure: B2B: headline last baseline -> first body baseline (no deck, byline or photo between)

headline_to_photo.measure: headline last baseline -> photo top edge

deck_to_photo.measure: deck last baseline -> photo top edge

photo_to_body.measure: photo bottom edge -> first body baseline

photo_to_headline.measure: photo bottom edge -> headline first baseline (photo above its headline)

photo_to_caption.measure: photo bottom edge -> caption first baseline

body_to_headline_no_rule.measure: B2B: last body baseline of the story above -> headline first baseline

body_to_body_between_runs.measure: B2B across a gap in one column (blank line or a run break)

box_top_to_first_baseline.measure: box top edge -> first baseline inside

last_baseline_to_box_bottom.measure: last baseline inside -> box bottom edge

box_bottom_to_headline.measure: box bottom edge -> headline first baseline

box_bottom_to_body.measure: box bottom edge -> first body baseline

headline_to_body_runin_dateline.measure: B2B; the first body line opens with a run-in dateline

kicker_to_headline.measure: B2B: kicker baseline -> headline first baseline (K1/K3)

reversed_label_to_headline.measure: B2B: reversed label baseline -> headline first baseline

story_separation_with_rule.measure: last body baseline (or photo bottom) above -> rule -> headline first baseline, total

spacing.rule: neighbours in the 8-column stacks; pairs farther than 12.0 body leadings or overlapping are not spacing evidence; L = the body leading of the text involved, else the page's body leading

vertical_rules.note: no column rules: gutters are white

box_categories.photo_frame: stroked box on a photo's edges
box_categories.label_panel: tinted (not white) fill <= 15 mm tall holding a short label
box_categories.tint_panel: tinted (not white) fill taller than 15 mm holding text
box_categories.inset_label: light panel laid on a darker box (a tab label: dark frame, light panel, dark text)
box_categories.white_mask: white fill without stroke holding text (knock-out)
box_categories.frame_or_tab: box with no text of its own (empty frames, the dark tab under an inset label, artwork rectangles)

headline_to_photo.measure: headline last baseline -> photo top edge

deck_to_photo.measure: deck last baseline -> photo top edge

photo_to_body.measure: photo bottom edge -> first body baseline

photo_to_headline.measure: photo bottom edge -> headline first baseline (photo above its headline)

photo_to_caption.measure: photo bottom edge -> caption first baseline

images.rule: photos = images >= 15 x 10 mm that are not furniture, recurring or inside an ad block; widths fitted to the 8-column spans and to k text columns of the body frame directly below or above the photo (gutter between)

furniture.rule: furniture = text repeated at the same position (+-2.0 mm) in >= 3 editions (static), or one font and size at one position with changing text inside the top block or at the page foot (variable: date line, folio)

composition.rule: lead story = the page's largest main headline (ties: wider span, higher); vertical position = (first baseline - editorial top) / editorial height; areas on a 1 mm raster, priority ad > furniture > photo > text > graphics

default.line_count: an input from the page plan (the owner fixes it before the headline is written)
default.why: 'fill' (earlier lines as full as possible, Knuth-Plass ragged-right) won the pre-registered selection on the calibration editions; the later editions tie it with 'balanced', and no page, span, size or alignment group separates the shapes reliably, so the paper's own rule (by page and by designer) has to be set per page

headline_shape.rule: printed: Devanagari main headlines with >= 2 lines; balance = shortest / longest line; first line longest = longer than every other line by > 1 mm; fill = longest line / span. choice: head1 rows that are comparable, multi-line and have >= 2 feasible layouts (V1 rules; FIXED = fewest lines, *_N = printed line count); exact = the printed breaks.

other_practice.hyphenation: line-end hyphens are rare: 3.4 unverified candidates per 100 body lines (docs/phase0/EXP_PUBLISHED_1.md section 12)

latin_section.note: the dual-language editions carry a Latin-script section with its own masthead (flip format); reported apart

where.value: between stories (above a headline, kicker, panel or photo)

headline_shape.line_count: an input from the page plan (the owner fixes it before the headline is written)

checks.check: gutter (mm), measured directly between adjacent columns
checks.reference_source: headline_practice.json grid estimate; ours is an independent measurement
EXP_PUBLISHED_1.md section 12: median 12 pt on 13 pt

body_line_steps.what: pixel step between headstrokes of consecutive body lines minus the measured baseline step

headstroke_above_baseline_em.what: constant if the measured baselines are right

limitations: One-off display ads placed as a single picture cannot be told from photos by geometry; recurring ads are found by recurrence, and stand-alone photos >= 40 x 40 mm are counted as possible ads (images.possible_one_off_ads).
Captions are rare in this paper (most photos run without one), so caption specs rest on few frames.
Text ink extents use the em box (0.75 em above, 0.25 em below the baseline), not glyph outlines; distances between text are baseline to baseline, which is exact.
Display tracking comes from published1/headline_practice.json (all pages, its own role rules); body tracking and word space from the measured body frames.
Which designer made a page is not in the files: running-head variants are reported as variants, not as designers.
Headline-shape evidence is limited to the head1 'choice' headlines (a few dozen per split); differences under about 20 points cannot be detected.
Photo content (crops, cut-outs, colour) and image resolution are not analysed.
Page types follow the nameplate: in the dual-language (flip-format) editions each language section has its own front.
